sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! When I moved the cursor left and clicked on the top-left cell (which was green), it changed to gray (g). So the cursor position affects what color the cell changes to:
- Cursor at right end: clicks change cells to green (N)
- Cursor at left position: clicks change cells to gray (g)
Current grid:
```
g N g
W g W
g W g
```
The cursor is now at cols 23-26 (left side of the bar). Let me check what color mode this corresponds to. The cursor shows:
- Rows 19-20: bbSS (blue then sky blue)
- Rows 21-22: bbSS (blue then sky blue)
Wait, looking at the bar output:
```
Row 19: 'ggggggbbSSggggggggggggggg'
Row 20: 'ggggggbbSSggggggggggggggg'
Row 21: 'BBBBBBbbSSggggggggggggggg'
Row 22: 'BBBBBBbbSSggggggggggggggg'
```
The cursor is at cols 23-26 with pattern bbSS. Previously at the right end, it was SSbb. So the cursor orientation flipped when I moved it.
Actually, let me reconsider. The cursor might have different "modes" based on its position or orientation:
- Mode 1 (cursor at right, SS on top): paints green (N)
- Mode 2 (cursor at left, bb on top): paints gray (g)
Or maybe the cursor color directly determines the paint color. The cursor has blue (b) and sky blue (S) components. When I click:
- With cursor showing bbSS (blue dominant): paints gray
- With cursor showing SSbb (sky blue dominant): paints green
Let me test this theory by moving the cursor to different positions and clicking. But first, let me think about the target pattern.
The purple cross pattern:
```
  pp  -> center column (cols 15-16 in the panel)
  pp
pp  pp -> left and right columns
pp  pp
  pp
  pp
```
This maps to a 3x3 grid as:
```
. X .   -> top-center
X . X   -> middle-left and middle-right
. X .   -> bottom-center
```
Where X = "active" (green) and . = "inactive" (gray or white).
Current grid:
```
g N g   -> top-center is green (correct!)
W g W   -> middle-left and middle-right are white (need green)
g W g   -> bottom-center is white (need green)
```
So I need to:
1. Keep top-center green (already correct)
2. Change middle-left to green
3. Change middle-right to green
4. Change bottom-center to green
5. Make sure other cells are non-green (they already are)
To paint green, I need the cursor in the "green mode" (right end position). Let me move the cursor right and click the needed cells.
But wait, I also need to be careful about the cells that are currently white (W). When I click them with the green mode, they should turn green. And when I click with the gray mode, they turn gray. So I can use the cursor to select which color to apply.
Let me move the cursor to the right and click the three cells that need to be green.
